note: What activate_release.py may do (PLT-14, #21; D-74, D-26, D-27). Exactly one format transition is admitted, from the D-19 baseline formats (staging.json's live_versions) to #19's formats, and only through an activation plan bound to one release, these targets, one state snapshot and this transition. A normal preflight still refuses it. No wildcard compatibility: every other format keeps the strict check. The targets are D-26's seven managed targets, by name, and no others.

transition.name: d19-baseline-to-19
transition.covers: #19's declared format delta: two write versions raised (old versions still read), its new authority interface and state, its two read-only host interfaces, the bootstrap record PLT-14 hands the bridge, and writer admission's maintenance record (#23, #24; #21 amendment 4, G-3), which only the activation's fenced operation writes

first_writes.note: The first new-format write, after which an automatic return to pre-#19 code is refused (D-74). The controller judges each from the state directory alone, never from its journal, and never opens the outbox database.
first_writes.outbox-db/1: outbox.db, or any of its -wal, -shm or -journal files, exists in the chat state directory
first_writes.outbox/2: the outbox.d directory, or the refusal sink refused.d (writer admission's refused writes, which only new code reads), exists in the chat state directory
first_writes.delivery-records/2: dead-letters.jsonl holds a record carrying version or supersedes

bootstrap.note: The one declared read input #21's owner amendment (2026-10-11) adds. Its canonical bytes are derived from the sealed activation plan; the controller publishes them privately (mode 0600) without replacing anything, journals D, their sha256, and only then binds the chat-bridge LaunchAgent with exactly --activation-bootstrap sha256:<D>. Read only by the bridge, whose authority alone validates it against D and commits the designations, before serving, import or recovery (D-74, D-26). A rollback leaves it in place.
